sinks.name: TA_InvokeCommandEntryPoint
sinks.reason: May carry per-session state/handles that influence access control and operations on sensitive data.

sinks.name: TA_InvokeCommandEntryPoint
sinks.reason: Selects which command/operation is executed, affecting control flow and security-relevant behavior.

sinks.name: TA_InvokeCommandEntryPoint
sinks.reason: Determines how parameters are interpreted (memrefs/values), impacting parsing and validation of untrusted input.

sinks.name: TA_InvokeCommandEntryPoint
sinks.reason: Primary carrier of client-supplied input and TA output; typically read, written, compared, and transformed within command handlers.

sinks.name: TA_OpenSessionEntryPoint
sinks.reason: May influence session setup logic and authorization decisions.
sinks.role: connection method identifier / access control input

sinks.name: TA_OpenSessionEntryPoint
sinks.reason: Carries untrusted data (values/memrefs) that the TA may read/validate/transform during session initialization.

sinks.name: TA_OpenSessionEntryPoint
sinks.reason: TA writes session state pointer/handle which affects subsequent command handling and security context.

sinks.name: TEE_AllocateTransientObject
sinks.reason: Determines what kind of cryptographic/key object is created, affecting how sensitive material may be stored/used.

sinks.name: TEE_AllocateTransientObject
sinks.reason: Controls the size/capacity of the transient object (often key size), impacting security properties and subsequent sensitive data handling.

sinks.name: TEE_AllocateTransientObject
sinks.reason: Returns a handle to a newly allocated object that will hold sensitive cryptographic material and be used in later operations.
sinks.role: output handle to allocated transient object

sinks.name: TEE_GenerateRandom
sinks.reason: function writes generated random data into caller-provided memory

sinks.name: TEE_GenerateRandom
sinks.reason: controls how much data is written to the output buffer, affecting security and memory safety
sinks.role: number of random bytes to generate

sinks.name: TEE_GetSystemTime
sinks.reason: receives time data written by the TEE, which can influence security decisions (e.g., time-based checks, token expiry) and is an external data source

sinks.name: TEE_InitRefAttribute
sinks.reason: written with attribute metadata including a reference to external data

sinks.name: TEE_InitRefAttribute
sinks.reason: supplies data reference that will be stored and later used by crypto/object operations

sinks.name: TEE_InitRefAttribute
sinks.reason: controls how much of the referenced data is considered; affects bounds and interpretation

sinks.name: TEE_InvokeTACommand

sinks.name: TEE_InvokeTACommand
sinks.reason: Controls which operation is executed, influencing how provided data is interpreted/processed

sinks.name: TEE_InvokeTACommand
sinks.reason: Carries input/output data buffers and parameter types that are read/written/transformed by the invoked command

sinks.name: TEE_MACComputeFinal
sinks.reason: Determines key and internal state used to process input and produce MAC output

sinks.name: TEE_MACComputeFinal
sinks.reason: Reads caller-controlled data to be authenticated (MAC computed over it)

sinks.name: TEE_MACComputeFinal
sinks.reason: Controls how many bytes are read from the input buffer

sinks.name: TEE_MACComputeFinal
sinks.reason: Writes computed MAC/tag bytes to caller-provided memory

sinks.name: TEE_MACComputeFinal
sinks.reason: Reads expected output size and writes actual produced MAC length

sinks.name: TEE_MACInit
sinks.reason: Initializes cryptographic MAC state that will be used to process key/material and data in subsequent update/final calls

sinks.name: TEE_MACInit
sinks.reason: IV/nonce is security-sensitive input that influences MAC computation and must be handled correctly

sinks.name: TEE_MACInit
sinks.reason: Controls how many bytes are read from the IV/nonce buffer

sinks.name: TEE_OpenPersistentObject
sinks.reason: Identifier bytes are read to locate/select a stored persistent object, influencing which secure data is accessed.

sinks.name: TEE_OpenPersistentObject
sinks.reason: Determines how many bytes from the identifier buffer are consumed, affecting the selection of the persistent object.

sinks.name: TEE_OpenPersistentObject
sinks.reason: Receives a handle granting access to persistent storage content; enables subsequent reads/writes of security-sensitive data.

sinks.name: TEE_OpenTASession
sinks.reason: Selects which Trusted Application to connect to; influences security context and access control.

sinks.name: TEE_OpenTASession
sinks.reason: Controls authentication/authorization mechanism used for the session.

sinks.name: TEE_OpenTASession
sinks.reason: May carry identity or credentials used to authenticate when opening the session.

sinks.name: TEE_OpenTASession
sinks.reason: Carries data exchanged during session open; may include sensitive parameters passed to the TA.

sinks.name: TEE_PopulateTransientObject
sinks.reason: object is populated/modified with provided attributes, affecting stored sensitive key/material state

sinks.name: TEE_PopulateTransientObject
sinks.reason: contains key material or other sensitive attributes that are read and used to populate the object

sinks.name: TEE_PopulateTransientObject
sinks.reason: controls how many attributes are read from the attribute array, influencing data processing

sinks.name: TEE_ReadObjectData
sinks.reason: selects the persistent object whose contents will be read

sinks.name: TEE_ReadObjectData
sinks.reason: receives data read from the object

sinks.name: TEE_ReadObjectData
sinks.reason: controls how much object data is copied into the output buffer

sinks.name: TEE_ReadObjectData
sinks.reason: returns how many bytes were actually read, reflecting data flow

sinks.name: TEE_SetOperationKey
sinks.reason: the operation context is updated/configured with a key, affecting subsequent cryptographic processing

sinks.name: TEE_SetOperationKey
sinks.reason: provides the cryptographic key material that will be read and bound to the operation
sinks.role: key handle / key object containing secret key material

sinks.reason: provides bytes to be copied; reads potentially sensitive or tainted data
